requirements.requirement: New user passwords on node1 must require at least 12 characters
requirements.summary: pwquality.conf.d/99-complexity.conf sets minlen=12. Functional tests confirm an 11-char/3-class password is rejected (exit 10) while a 12-char/3-class password is accepted (exit 0), directly demonstrating the length floor is enforced, both pre- and post-restart.

requirements.requirement: New user passwords on node1 must require at least 3 different character classes
requirements.summary: Config sets minclass=3. Functional tests show a 12-char/2-class password is rejected (exit 10) while a 12-char/3-class password is accepted (exit 0), directly demonstrating the class-count requirement is enforced, both pre- and post-restart.

requirements.requirement: Policy applies to actual password-change flow (not just a standalone quality checker) and persists across restart
requirements.summary: pam_pwquality is confirmed wired into system-auth/password-auth before configuration, and enforcement was verified via real 'passwd' invocations as a non-root user rather than only pwscore. The config file content and enforcement behavior were re-verified identically after a full node restart with a changed boot_id.

overall_summary: The executor configured pam_pwquality with minlen=12/minclass=3 on node1 and directly demonstrated enforcement (boundary cases at 11-char/3-class and 12-char/2-class both correctly rejected, 12-char/3-class accepted) via real non-root passwd invocations, both before and after a full node restart with a confirmed changed boot_id, satisfying the task contract and the independent restart-evidence protocol. Hygiene is good overall; the only blemish is a small leftover /tmp/reboot.log file from the reboot mechanism, and test users were properly cleaned up (with one retry needed due to a stale login session).
limitations: Single-node topology means the restart protocol's cluster-state recovery check is not applicable; only service (sshd) and data (policy file) recovery could be directly observed.
/tmp/reboot.log is minor unreviewed residue from the reboot mechanism; its contents were not inspected for sensitive data, though it is low-risk given it only logs the reboot invocation.

operational_hygiene.summary: Test users pwtestuser and pwtestuser2 were created to functionally validate the policy and both were deleted afterward (cmd-1793716e7712461b initial userdel failed because a process was still attached, corrected by cmd-4119d7b257d8481f with pkill+userdel, which succeeded; pwtestuser2 cleanup in cmd-b5ffec178a904b18 succeeded on the same retry pattern) — a bounded, low-risk, fully-reverted mutation tied directly to verifying the task outcome. One minor residue remains: /tmp/reboot.log, created by the backgrounded reboot command (cmd-cae637d0969b4441) and still present in the after-executor snapshot; it is a tiny, inert log file with no functional impact but was not cleaned up. No failed services, no damaged package state, and no new/changed listening sockets (only PIDs differ due to the restart) were observed between after-prepare and after-executor snapshots.
